findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime, a datetime. The endpoint orders by -datetime, and build_cursor calls the key on every non-empty page. So every non-empty page with ?optimized_pagination=true from an eligible user raises TypeError, which paginate() does not catch, and the endpoint returns 500.
findings.evidence: Executed by the seats: python3 -c "import math,datetime; math.floor(datetime.datetime.now())" -> TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime. The method copies Paginator.get_item_key, not DateTimePaginator's epoch-ms conversion. No test covers optimized_pagination.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats with an executed repro of the core failure. Red test before fixing: in tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py, as owner, create one AuditLogEntry, GET with qs_params={'optimized_pagination': 'true'}, expect 200 (currently 500).

findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor.value with no datetime conversion. build_queryset then emits datetime <= <int>, a timestamptz-vs-integer comparison. Any cursored request on the optimized path errors or pages wrongly, and cursors from DateTimePaginator (epoch-ms) are incompatible.
findings.evidence: Reasoned by all three seats, not executed. DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor (paginator.py:238-241) does the conversion the new class omits.
findings.reason: Raised by 3 seats. Severity normalised to Critical (2 of 3 seats; a client-reachable 500 on every cursored request). Unverified until red: GET with optimized_pagination=true and a valid next cursor from a populated page, expect 200 with correct rows.

findings.claim: enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access runs on every request, even without the opt-in flag. member is None for callers with no membership, such as legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration/sentry-app proxy users with org:write. Those callers now get an AttributeError and a 500 on the default, previously working path.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is documented nullable (organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346). Internal-integration proxy users have no OrganizationMember row (sentry_apps/logic.py:351-353). Only an is_superuser short-circuit avoids the dereference.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats (mattpocock in #6, ponytail as a side note). Normalised to Critical: a regression on the default path of an existing endpoint that needs no opt-in. Red test: call the endpoint with an internal-integration token that has org:write and no flag, expect 200 (reasoned to return 500).

findings.claim: The admin gate checks the raw request.user.is_superuser DB flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), which OrganizationAuditPermission uses. A user with the flag but no active superuser session gets the 'admin' path.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. bases/organization.py:124 uses is_active_superuser(request). The queryset stays scoped to organization_id, and the gate only switches paginators, so current impact is limited.
findings.reason: Raised by 3 seats. Normalised to Minor (2 of 3 seats; low impact because the gated path only selects a paginator). Use is_active_superuser(request), or drop the gate along with the optimized path.

findings.claim: The 'advanced' branch passes a user-controlled negative cursor.offset into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django (>=5.2.1) raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), which is not a BadPaginationError, so any cursor such as 0:-10:0 with optimized_pagination=true returns 500. The advertised feature cannot work, and its comments (ORM 'properly handles negative slicing', 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are false or describe a hazardous intent.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from Django QuerySet.__getitem__ and the pinned Django version (requirements-frozen.txt:36). Not executed: Django is not installed locally per superpowers.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats. Red test: as org owner, GET ...audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-10:0, expect 400 (reasoned 500). Django blocks the slice, so no data leak today.

findings.claim: The patch changes shared BasePaginator.get_result, which every Paginator, DateTimePaginator and other subclass uses. start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset silently clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0 instead of failing, while negative prev-cursor offsets still reach the slice and 500. The audit-log feature does not need the change, nothing tests it, and its comment ('the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions') is false.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the diff hunk at paginator.py:179-184 and Django slicing semantics. open-code-review gives no failing command for the clamp itself.
findings.reason: Raised by 4 seats. Revert the hunk to the original two lines. If negative offsets need rejecting, do it at Cursor.from_string/get_cursor_from_request, which already map ValueError to 400. Red test: BasePaginator with a non-prev cursor at a negative offset must not silently return page 0; on the pinned code it does.

findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near line-for-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result: same queryset, count and slice. Its only additions are broken (key, cursor conversion, negative-offset branch). The class delivers no performance improvement despite the commit title, and DateTimePaginator already serves the endpoint. The class can be deleted.
